issue_paraphrase: When a .NET application's dependency graph file contains several sibling projects (typical for solutions where the root app and multiple helper projects are all recorded as libraries, and nothing but the reference graph distinguishes them), the scanner treats the first-listed project as the root application and silently omits every other project and its transitive dependencies from the reported packages. The root should be identified as the project no other library references, not by its position in the file.
fix_summary: Replaced 'first project wins' root selection with rootProject(): collects all libraries of type project, builds the set of all package IDs referenced from any library's targets/dependencies, and marks as root the single unreferenced project (RelationshipRoot), all other projects RelationshipWorkspace; if zero or multiple candidates exist it logs and returns a non-root parse instead of guessing. Direct dependencies are then looked up under the resolved root project ID.
notes: Solid mid-size fix (~+36 source lines incl. helper + two fixtures). Same env caveats as the other entries: GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 mandatory, run the single module with `go test`, first run downloads ~1GB of pinned deps. Verification logs in container trivy-miner: /tmp/dotnet_parent.log and /tmp/dotnet_fix.log.

issue_paraphrase: Dependency names declared in the PEP 621 style of a Python pyproject.toml are recorded exactly as typed (e.g. 'Flask' instead of 'flask', 'typing_extensions' instead of 'typing-extensions', 'ruamel.yaml' instead of 'ruamel-yaml'), so the names do not line up with the normalized names produced by other Python lockfiles. A package can therefore be reported under different spellings in different parts of the same scan, breaking dependency-name matching between the project manifest and the lockfile.
fix_summary: The PEP 621 'dependencies' name extraction now passes each parsed name through python.NormalizePkgName(name, true) (PEP 503 normalization: lowercase, runs of non-alphanumerics -> '-') before storing it in the dependency set, matching the normalization the poetry/pylock parsers already apply; the fixture now uses non-normalized spellings to prove the match.
notes: Small fix (2 source lines) but a real, user-visible correctness bug with the project's own regression coverage. Same env caveats as the other entries (GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2, single-module `go test`, ~1GB first download). Verification logs in container trivy-miner: /tmp/pyp_parent.log and /tmp/pyp_fix.log.

issue_paraphrase: For projects managed by a pnpm release that writes its YAML lockfile as multiple documents - the first holding the package manager's own environment (pnpm itself and its per-platform binary packages), a later one the actual project dependencies - the scanner decodes only the first document, so it reports the package manager's internal packages as if they were the project's dependencies, flooding the SBOM with pnpm's machinery while the real project dependency is missing from the report.
fix_summary: The pnpm YAML parser now loops over all YAML documents, skipping any document that is the pnpm environment lockfile (detected via the new isEnvLockfile() on the lockfile's importers, which checks for configDependencies/packageManagerDependencies fields) and parsing the first non-environment document; an empty/env-only file returns no packages.
notes: Good size (~44 source/test lines + 221-line fixture). Fixture produced by real pnpm 11.7.0 output as documented in the testcase comment. Same env caveats as the other entries (GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2, single-module `go test`, ~1GB first download; the pnpm module test suite runs in ~0.05s after build).
